claims.text: Laser cladding can deposit a WC-reinforced HEA surface layer.
Approximately 0.2 mass % WC is a small, optimized reinforcement content for the cladded layer.
WC-reinforced laser cladding will induce a dynamic, self-adaptive nanostructured tribolayer during sliding.
Incorporated WC partially decomposes in the HEA cladding layer.
WC incorporation and decomposition cause lattice distortion and grain refinement in the cladding layer.
The modified layer develops a nanohierarchical architecture containing ultrafine grains and dispersed nanoprecipitates.
A nanohierarchical grain-and-precipitate architecture promotes adaptive friction-interface protection and formation of a nanocrystalline glaze during wear.
WC-derived species facilitate in situ formation of a lubricious glaze or ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
Formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer is linked to low friction and low wear in an HEA.
The glaze layer lowers friction by acting as a barrier to dislocation motion.
The engineered tribolayer minimizes wear by distributing contact stresses over a larger area.
The treatment will reduce coefficient of friction by approximately 25–30% relative to the untreated HEA.
The treatment will reduce wear rate by at least a factor of two relative to the untreated HEA.
Both friction and wear improvements will be maintained from room temperature through at least 800 °C.
An untreated CoCrFeMnNi HEA can exhibit a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.3 in ultra-high vacuum.
An untreated coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi HEA can exhibit a wear rate on the order of 10^-6 mm3/N-m in an inert environment.
The benefits will persist as long as the cladding layer remains intact and its nanohierarchical structure is preserved.
Temperature spikes, aggressive corrosion, or mechanical impacts that disrupt the cladding can negate its tribological benefits.
